fixes.system: src/render/materials.js:786 (texture2D(uPaperTex, sPx*0.001953125)) and getPaperTexture() in src/render/textures.js
fixes.problem: MEASURE (c), paper-grain orientation anisotropy, band-limited to 1.5-4 px, median of 48 random 32-px tiles per region. LIT: stone face anisotropy 0.937 (p90 0.972), dominant orientation 97 deg in 16/48 tiles; house wall 0.944 dom 7 deg; lit grass 0.779; sky 0.836 dom 97 deg. SHADOWED: arch-1 intrados 0.951 dom 112 deg; arch-2 intrados 0.944 dom 97 deg; shaded bank 0.925; water 0.905. Lit and shadowed are statistically identical (0.94 vs 0.95) and every one of the eight regions peaks at the same 3 cycles/32 px = 10.7 px period. Cold-press fibre is isotropic (anisotropy <0.30); this is a directionally locked, near-vertical machine ruling - the round-3 'machine-ruled paper' was implemented literally and it is the wrong substrate. Worse, sPx*0.001953125 is a 512-px SCREEN-SPACE tile: sky residual self-correlation is r=0.192 at horizontal lag 512 against -0.005 to +0.003 at lags 64/128/256/341/683, i.e. the sheet visibly repeats 3.75 times across the frame - a repeating texture with an obvious tiling period, an automatic rejection. Amplitude is also windowed wrong: residual RMS runs 11.03 at L80-100 monotonically down to 1.01 at L220-240, so the grain is a shadow dirt-multiply, not a substrate that peaks at midtones.
fixes.change: Rebuild getPaperTexture() as a 3-octave isotropic value-noise cold-press (equal energy in all 12 orientation bins, target anisotropy <0.25) at 1024x1024, sample it with a per-fragment 4-way rotated lookup (rotate uv by 90*floor(hash(floor(sPx/512))*4) deg) so the 512 tile cannot phase-align with itself, and replace vcPaperMidScene with a true midtone window peaking at L=0.55 and falling to 0 below L=0.20 and above L=0.85. Verification: per-region anisotropy median <0.35 on both a lit and a shadowed patch, sky self-correlation at lag 512 below 0.05, and residual RMS in the L80-100 decile below 5 LSB while the L140-180 decile stays above 6.

fixes.system: src/world/worldMaterials.js:180-182 (npShade) applied to the tank pass in src/actors/tank.js
fixes.problem: npShade = dot(directDiffuse + indirectDiffuse, vec3(0.3333)) / (npLum*uSunLum) lets a large uniform indirect term swamp N.L, so surface orientation stops driving the band index. Measured on the hero subject: turret roof (620-900, 390-430) lum 108, track-guard top (300-500, 560-600) lum 88, vertical hull side (700-1100, 620-700) lum 118, front glacis lum 115 - up-facing planes are 10-30 LSB DARKER than vertical ones, impossible under a sky. The whole tank spans 88-118 lum inside hue 240-253, i.e. one band, so it is a flat violet cutout and the camo blotches are the only thing separating it from the wall behind it.
fixes.change: Split the terms before quantising: ndl = max(dot(normalize(normal), normalize(uSunDirView)), 0.0); npShade = ndl * shadowMask * 1.05 + skyOcclusion * 0.16, and drop indirectDiffuse out of the numerator entirely (it may still tint npShadeCol). Clamp the indirect contribution to <=0.16 so it can never move a fragment by more than half a band. Verification: turret roof mean lum must exceed vertical hull side mean lum by >=35 LSB, the tank must occupy >=3 distinct band indices, and the frame-wide ratio of mean lum on up-facing normals to vertical normals must be >=1.25.

fixes.system: src/world/worldMaterials.js:155-159 (bandify) and :195-201 (npCol mix) + src/world/terrain.js:523 (AO baked into vertex colour)
fixes.problem: Nothing in the pipeline is flat. bandify quantises npShade, but npBase carries a continuous per-vertex AO ramp and continuous detail textures that are multiplied back in at :195-201, and mix(npShadeCol, npMidCol, smoothstep(0.05,0.58,npQ)) re-interpolates on top. Result: 0 plateaus of >=12 samples within +-2 LSB on the median-filtered dirt road (79->218), foreground road (94->159), retaining wall (100->154), soldier head and tank turret; the soldier's leg fills 44 of 64 four-LSB luminance buckets with a modal bucket of 8.2%. The source is byte-identical to round 2 here.
fixes.change: Quantise the colour, not just the lighting scalar: int bi = int(floor(npQ*uBands + 0.001)); build the wash from a 4-entry ramp indexed by bi whose entries derive from a LOW-FREQUENCY npBase only (albedo through a 12 px blur, or the vertex colour with AO stripped) so no continuous term survives the quantiser. In terrain.js:523 replace _col.lerp(shadeTint,(1-ao)*0.40) with ao = floor(ao*3.0+0.5)/3.0 before the lerp. Then make the boundary a pigment edge: float aa = fwidth(sc)*0.9; float w = max(uEdge, aa); smoothstep(0.5-w, 0.5+w, fr), and add a third warp octave at npPx*0.045 weighted 0.25 into npWarp so boundaries break into 6-15 px lobes. Verification: a 60-row median profile down the road at x1380-1520 must contain >=3 plateaus of >=12 samples within +-2 LSB covering >=55% of the profile; the soldier's leg must occupy <=14 of 64 four-LSB buckets with a modal bucket >=18%; no lit/shade transition may complete in under 2 px.

fixes.system: src/world/vegetation.js (grass instance placement) + src/world/worldMaterials.js:220-224 (hatch sines)
fixes.problem: The foreground road is covered by a machine-ruled lattice. ACF of the 9 px high-pass at (300-760, 920-1060) peaks at lag 10 px in x, r=0.203, harmonic 19 px, and 7 px in y; the field at (1500-1700, 940-1050) peaks at 8 px, r=0.237. In the hatch block, quantise the stroke index si = floor((npPx.x*0.819+npPx.y*0.574)*0.52/3.14159), hash it, and use the hash to offset phase, scale amplitude 0.55-1.0 and cut strokes into 20-70 px segments with smoothstep ends; replace smoothstep(0.24,0.72,npL1) with smoothstep(0.45,0.55,npL1)*(0.6+0.4*grain). Raise the gate to 1.0 - smoothstep(1.35, 2.4, npBi) so band 2 also receives hatch. Verification: ACF of any 400x140 ground patch must show no peak above r=0.09 for lags 4-40 px; mean continuous hatch run-length below 80 px with stroke-amplitude sd above 25% of mean; the tank's darkest 20% of pixels must show high-pass sd >=4 from hatch modulation.

fixes.change: Split the single 26 m ortho box into two cascades (8 m near, 40 m far) and centre the near box on the camera-forward ground intersection at 4 m rather than on the followLambda target; drop shadow.bias to -0.0004 with normalBias 0.012 to kill the offset. Add a 0.35 m radial contact-AO decal parented to each actor's lowest foot bone. Verification: mean luma in a 60x30 box directly beneath each actor's lowest vertex must be >=18 LSB below the open-plaza mean at the same screen depth.

fixes.system: src/world/worldMaterials.js:195 npShadeCol / :311 uShadeTint (0x4b4270) and its routing to stucco, roof and terrain materials
fixes.problem: The round-3 cool-shade fix landed on only two of nine materials. But cream stucco -4.2 deg (39.2 -> 35.0, shade B-R -74), roof tile -4.6 deg, plaza paving -13.4 deg (37.9 -> 24.5, shade B-R -59), grass only +17.0 with blue still the lowest channel. fixes.change: Apply the npShadeCol.b = max(npShadeCol.b, npShadeCol.r*1.10) clamp in the shared NPR body for EVERY material instance (stucco, pantile, paving, grass), and replace the fixed 0x4b4270 with a per-albedo rotation - shade hue = albedo hue + 45 deg toward 255 deg, chroma 0.22 - so brick shades violet-red and grass shades blue-green instead of everything collapsing on one pole. Verification: for every material patch, shade(B-R) must exceed lit(B-R) by >=25, and no mid band may exceed hue 280.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js band quantiser (uBands :1257/:1492, uBandBleed :1267) and the hatch block at :688-696
fixes.problem: Terrain has no bands and characters have too many. Blurred-luma mode counts: lit plaza (y680-820, x650-1150) = 2 modes over a 161 LSB range with flat(|dL/dx|<0.4) = 0.38; near plaza = 1 mode; left grass bank = 1 mode; lit cream wall = 1 mode. Character: hero torso+leg = 6 modes (75/93/129/145/163/181), right soldier body = 6 modes, and the boundaries are single-pixel jumps of 20.1 to 72.9 LSB, 8 or more per 160 px scan - hard aliased steps, not bled pigment. fixes.change: Set CFG.render.bands to 4 on world materials, and drive the band boundary offset from the paper G-channel mottle at 2.5x the current bandBleed so each edge wobbles over 4-7 px instead of snapping on one texel; on skinned materials clamp bands to 3 and prefilter the half-Lambert drive with a 2-px screen-space median so the shard field collapses. Re-enable the hatch by raising its opacity until it is measurable. Verification: a 500x140 plaza patch must return 3 +/- 1 histogram modes with flat fraction >=0.6; no 160-px character scan may contain more than 4 jumps >18 LSB; and the darkest band on any surface must show >=25:1 directional power at 45 deg (the hatch) with a 3-5 px stroke period.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js:900-912 paper composite (uPaperStrength 0.42, fibre gain 1.15) + src/core/config.js:20

Inside every character band the residual is visually flat.
fixes.change: Raise CFG.render.paperStrength 0.42 -> 0.85 and the fibre gain at :907 from 1.15 to 1.90; replace mid = pow(1-abs(l*2-1), 0.75) with a two-sided smoothstep(0.10,0.40,l)*smoothstep(0.95,0.66,l) so the tooth peaks at L=140-180 and is gone above L=220; and remove the skinned-pass exclusion so the multiply covers actors and sky alike. dusk.tell: The focal figure is a faceless armature: the 396px-tall foreground soldier has an unmodelled ovoid head with zero facial features, no hands, and no left arm at all — the near shoulder pauldron simply terminates and the silhouette runs straight down the flank — while a rectangular pouch shelf overhangs the hip with a hard 90 degree corner and both thighs fuse into one trapezoidal mass, and a 4-level k-means fit to his 5x5-median luminance puts only 16.1% of his pixels within +/-2.5 L of any band centre (terrain 39.5%, needs >85% for real quantised watercolour), so he reads as an untextured mannequin with continuous PBR falloff rather than a painted character.

fixes.system: src/actors/character.js (head/face build, arm chain, pouch, thigh split) + src/actors/rig.js skin weights
fixes.problem: ROUND 3'S NAMED TARGET DID NOT LAND. Foreground soldier, silhouette measured from a b>g-3 mask over x440-640 / y600-1030: head 44px wide x ~60px tall at y616-676, figure 396px to the boot sole (6.6 heads, acceptable), but the head carries no eye/brow/nose/mouth/ear geometry and no hairline — it is one violet-grey ovoid. Silhouette width goes 45px at y=630 (head), 113px at y=690 (shoulders), then 82-91px at y=720-750 with NO separate arm mass on the viewer-left side at any row: the arm is absent, not occluded. The viewer-right arm is a horizontal stub ending in a mitten with an orange sausage (RGB ~(150,110,70)) for a weapon; no fingers, no trigger hand, no sling. Legs are one mass from crotch to knee. The hip pouch is an axis-aligned box overhanging by ~14px with an unbevelled corner. The mid-field soldier (x822-862) and the tank crewman (x1265-1310) are the same puppet: egg head, no hands, and the crewman has no body below the hull line.
fixes.change: Build the head as a proper skull: brow ridge, nose wedge, eye sockets at 0.46 head height, mouth line, and a scalp-UV-masked hair shell clamped to v>=0.62; give it a modelled neck cylinder with a collar. Rebuild BOTH arm chains from clavicle->humerus->forearm->hand with a 5-bone hand (thumb opposed on the grip) and bind the rifle to the hand, not to a floating socket; verify by asserting the silhouette mask has TWO disjoint runs between y=shoulder+0.15h and y=shoulder+0.45h. Split the thighs with a 0.06m gap in bind pose and add a crotch seam edge loop so the legs read separately. Chamfer the pouch box at 0.02m and rotate it 12 degrees to follow the hip.

fixes.system: src/render/materials.js (band drive + vcQuantiseBands call) + src/render/shaderLib.js
fixes.problem: STILL NOT QUANTISED, third round running. Median-15 transects across shaded masses: terrain shaded field y=980 x=120-1150 gives 49 plateaus over 1030px at 58% coverage with steps of -2.9,+19.7,-26.3,+23.2,+9.2,... ; terrain vert x=250 y=700-1050 gives 15 plateaus with steps as small as -1.1 and -2.0 L; character vert x=505 gives 21 plateaus, mid soldier x=832 gives 11, tank crewman x=1280 gives 16. Four-level k-means band concentration (fraction of 5x5-median pixels within +/-2.5 L of a centre): terrain shaded field 39.5%, terrain lit slope 32.3%, mill mound 40.9%, soldier body 16.1%, soldier legs 36.5%, tank crew 29.7%, tank hull 21.4%. Real cold-press quantisation puts >85% there. What is on screen is a continuous ramp with grain multiplied over it.
fixes.change: Quantise the COMPOSITE luminance, not the light term, and do it after the band-index colour grade: y = vcLum(col); yq = vcQuantiseBands(y, 4.0, bandBleed) where the band edge is displaced by 0.09 * (vcFbm3(worldPos * 2.7) - 0.5) so boundaries bleed irregularly; then col *= yq / max(y, 0.02). Route actorBodyMaterial/actorGearMaterial and the terrain material through the same call with identical bands=4. Add a unit test that asserts the 4-level k-means concentration on any 100x100 single-material patch is >=0.85 within +/-2.5 L.

fixes.system: src/actors/tank.js (running gear, hull bottom) + src/render/lighting.js (shadow casters)
fixes.problem: AUTOMATIC REJECTION: the tank floats and casts no shadow. Ground luminance under the hull (x1400-1580, y725-750) is 83.62; open field at the same screen depth is 97.40 (left, x1050) and 84.34 (right, x1720) — a delta of only -7.25 L (-8.0%), i.e. ambient darkening, not a cast shadow. A real sun-cast tank shadow at this scale is -25 to -45 L. The hull bottom is a dead-straight horizontal line; there are no tracks, no road wheels, no return rollers, no idler and no sprocket, only five thin dark rectangular stubs with LIT grass visible between and beneath them. By comparison the mid-field soldier does get contact darkening (-27.9 L), so the tank is specifically excluded from the shadow pass. Nothing else in frame casts a directional shadow either: the two houses, the windmill and the power pole all sit on undarkened ground.
fixes.change: Model the running gear: 6 road wheels per side on a torsion-bar line, idler front, drive sprocket rear, 2 return rollers, and a continuous track band with 0.14m link pitch built as a swept path with a 3-degree sag between rollers. Set castShadow=true on the tank hull, turret, structure meshes and the power pole, and confirm they are in the cascade by asserting the under-hull ground sample is <=0.70x the open-field sample at the same depth. Add a hull-bottom ambient-occlusion decal projected onto the terrain at 1.15x the track footprint, 0.55 opacity, tinted toward the shade violet.

fixes.system: src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js paper composite + src/render/textures.js getPaperTexture
fixes.problem: PARTIAL FIX, WRONG MECHANISM. Credit first: the tone profile is no longer inverted — 9px high-pass std by tone bucket now reads 7.63 at L40-70, 12.36 at L90-110, 12.15 at L110-130, 6.37 at L150-170, 1.96 at L210-235, which is correctly midtone-peaked. But it is not a substrate. Lag-based autocorrelation of the 7px high-pass residual (Lx/Ly = lags before correlation falls below 0.3) swings by 35x depending on the surface and its lighting band: lit house wall 0.17 (ACx@2 = 0.09 vs ACy@2 = 0.67, vertically ruled), lit mill mound 0.17, lit far slope 0.50, lit sky 1.00, lit roof 1.00 — versus shaded tank hull 6.00 (ACx@2 = 0.50 vs ACy@2 = 0.14, horizontally ruled), shaded fg field ACx@2/ACy@2 = 0.23/0.01 = 23x, shaded soldier body 0.17, shaded house wall 2.00. A single sheet of cold-press cannot change fibre orientation per object and per lighting band. Separately the sky at L=173 still carries rms 5.83 with a radial spectral peak at 0.130 c/px (7.7px period) and 1.88x angular anisotropy — a coarse regular screen, not tooth.
fixes.change: Move the fibre to a single screen-space multiply applied ONCE at the end of the composite, after all material detail and after the hatch, sampled from one 2048 tileable cold-press map at 1:1 texel:pixel with a per-frame fixed offset (no UV scroll). Build getPaperTexture from summed isotropic Worley at 2.2px and 5.5px cell size plus 1/f noise — target a radial spectrum with no peak above 1.3x local mean anywhere in 0.05-0.45 c/px, and Lx/Ly within 0.85-1.18 on every flat patch. Keep the current midtone window. Then reduce the per-material detail maps that are currently masquerading as grain so no surface exceeds Lx/Ly 1.3.

fixes.system: src/world/vegetation.js (grass blade LOD, outline flag) + src/render/canvasRenderPipeline.js thin-geometry resolve
fixes.problem: AUTOMATIC REJECTION: aliased edges and firefly specks. In the 1250x480 foreground field (x0-1250, y600-1080), 24,152 pixels (4.03%) sit more than 18 L above their 5x5 local mean, 9,465 (1.58%) above 25 L and 3,669 (0.61%) above 35 L, with values like (231,233,164), (202,227,147), (216,228,158) — single-pixel specular sparkles on grass blade normals. At 4x nearest-neighbour every blade is a hard stair-stepped polygon with zero ink and zero anti-aliasing; the green/teal lit-shadow boundary across the field is a hard pixel-level dither edge with no pigment bleed. Round 2 asked for userData.outlineWidth = 0.4 on the near reed LOD; it is still absent.
fixes.change: Set userData.outlineWidth = 0.4 on the near grass LOD and route it through nprUniforms with bands=4 so blades take ink and quantised shading. Kill the sparkle by clamping the grass specular term to roughness >= 0.82 and zeroing it entirely below 0.004 screen-area coverage. Clamp thin geometry to a 1.6px minimum screen width with a coverage-weighted alpha so sub-pixel blades fade instead of aliasing, and apply a 2px pigment-bleed dilation along the lit/shade band boundary driven by the same vcFbm3 used for band bleed.

fixes.system: src/world/sky.js (SKY.zenith / SKY.horizon gradient) + src/render/lighting.js (sun elevation, shadow length)
fixes.problem: THIS SHOT IS NAMED 'dusk' AND CONTAINS NO DUSK. Sky at x1400-1700: L=163.6 at y=0, rising to 166.6 at y=160, falling to 144.7 at y=320 — 19 L of zenith-to-horizon delta and the wrong sign (bright at zenith, dark at horizon). Round 2 asked for >=45 L; still 26 L short and inverted. Sky hue 190.7 at sat 0.149 (a genuine fix — the ochre is gone) but the clouds are neutral white (212,214,201), there is no warm horizon band, no low-sun rim on any object, and no long shadow anywhere in frame. Aerial perspective, to be fair, now runs the right way: meanEdge 8.01 at 8m -> 5.46 at 50m -> 3.30 at 150m and saturation 0.299 -> 0.137, so haze itself is fixed.
fixes.change: Drop the sun to 9 degrees elevation at azimuth 108 degrees so cast shadows run 6.3x object height across the field. Set SKY.zenith = 0x53708c and SKY.horizon = 0xe6b688 with a gamma-2.2 vertical lerp giving >=55 L zenith-to-horizon and B > R at zenith / R > B below 12 degrees altitude. Tint cloud undersides with the horizon colour at 0.55 mix and add a rim term: rim = pow(1.0 - dot(N, V), 3.0) * sunColor * 0.8, gated to fragments whose N.dot(sunDir) > 0.15, so the soldiers and the tank pick up a warm edge against the sky.
